title: Y-coordinate of a turning point after reflection in the x-axis
source: Theory P1-2.6 Quick check 1 ((3,-4) maps to (3,4)); book Worked example 2.13 style, new numbers
stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) has a turning point at \(({p|int},-{q|int})\). The graph of \(y=-f(x)\) has a turning point at \(({p|int},k)\). What is the value of \(k\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: A reflection in the \(x\)-axis sends \(({p|int},-{q|int})\) to \(({p|int}, {K|int})\), so \(k={K|int}\).

title: X-coordinate of a turning point after reflection in the y-axis
source: Theory P1-2.6 Quick check 2 ((5,-2) maps to (-5,-2)); book Worked example 2.13 style, new numbers
stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) has a turning point at \(({p|int},-2)\). The graph of \(y=f(-x)\) has a turning point at \((k,-2)\). What is the value of \(k\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: A reflection in the \(y\)-axis sends \(({p|int},-2)\) to \(({K|int},-2)\), so \(k={K|int}\).

title: Y-intercept after a reflection of y=x squared plus c in the x-axis
source: Theory P1-2.6 Quick check 3 (y=x^2+7 reflects to y-intercept -7); book Key point 2.9, new numbers
stem: The graph of \(y=x^2+{c|int}\) is reflected in the \(x\)-axis. What is the \(y\)-intercept of the resulting graph?

title: Equation of the reflection of y=f(x) in the x-axis

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2020), Question 4(c) only, including the sentence that defines f. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Parts 4(a) and 4(b) are omitted (the range of f, and a vertical translation). The official diagram is not needed for part (c).

stem:
This question is 9709/11/M/J/20 Question 4(c), taken from the official QP.

The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x)=\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 2x+\dfrac{1}{2}\) for \(0\leqslant x\leqslant \pi\).

(c) State the equation of the curve which is the reflection of \(y=f(x)\) in the \(x\)-axis. Give your answer in the form \(y=a\cos 2x+b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants.  [1]

steps.name: B
steps.note: Official MS 4(c): B1 for y=-(3/2)cos 2x - 1/2. Independent: -((3/2)cos 2x + 1/2) = -(3/2)cos 2x - 1/2.
